`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The change is small in code but wide in effect. Every `GET /parcels` call without an explicit page size now returns up to twice as many rows.
- `MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 500` is the upper limit on what a client can request. The new default of 100 is well below it, so the default does not conflict with the limit.
- I checked that nothing else reads `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`. Other tests can still depend on 50 without naming it. An example is a test that creates 60 parcels and expects a second page. That is why I am running the whole suite and not only the one test.

Before this goes out, check these points:

- **No git repository.** This directory is not under version control. Your manager cannot see a diff, and you cannot revert quickly. If this is a scratch copy of the real repository, apply the change there through a normal PR.
- **Client effect.** Clients that do not send a page size will get larger responses. Their parsing does not change. If a client or dashboard counts on 50 items per page, it will see a difference. Response time and payload size for `/parcels` will also go up somewhat.
- **Rollout.** To limit the risk, deploy this alone, not together with other changes. Then watch `/parcels` latency and error rate after release. To roll back, change one line.
